event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: SWKS’s 2021-11-24 Form 10-K portrays COVID-19 as a clear, multi-faceted, and still-evolving threat.  Because the pandemic erupted only eighteen months before fiscal year-end, Time-Decay is minimal and the filing is replete with both historical damage (plant shutdowns, supply-chain delays, higher logistics costs, inventory builds, efficiency loss) and forward-looking warnings (continued supply constraints, labor attrition from vaccination mandates, demand volatility, macro-economic drag).  The narrative is specific—naming a two-week factory closure, discrete cost inflation and capacity shortfalls—yet largely un-quantified in dollars.  Management repeatedly acknowledges that many effects “continue” or “may continue,” underscoring an active, not hypothetical, risk posture.  Although the company lists certain mitigation steps (remote work, safety protocols, supplier engagement), these are framed as costly and only partially effective.  Taken together, the disclosures signal a high-severity, contemporaneous operational and financial risk consistent with 0-3-year recency, justifying upper-mid score levels on the micro-scorecards.

evidence_list.snippet: The effects of the global COVID-19 pandemic continue to adversely affect our business operations.

components.reason: Explicit statement that the pandemic is still causing adverse effects (‘continue to adversely affect’).
No detail on magnitude or specific business areas, reducing precision.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct, ongoing impact is acknowledged but without specifics, giving a moderate score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: The global COVID-19 pandemic—including the public health crisis, the measures taken by governments, businesses, and individuals in an effort to limit COVID-19’s spread, and the resulting global supply chain challenges—has adversely affected, and continues to adversely affect, our business operations.

components.reason: Connects pandemic and associated governmental measures to adverse impacts on operations.
Emphasises both historical and continuing nature of impact.
Mentions supply-chain challenges specifically.
Impact not quantified.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific linkage to supply-chain disruption and continuing adverse effects yields a solid risk score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced, and may continue to experience, disruptions to our supply chain and increased costs in connection with the sourcing of materials, components, equipment, assembly and test services, engineering support, shipping and logistics services, and other services, caused in part by the pandemic.

components.reason: States that supply-chain disruptions and cost increases have already occurred.
Lists multiple affected cost categories, showing breadth of impact.
Notes ongoing risk (‘may continue’).
No numerical quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete, multi-area cost and supply-chain impacts push the risk to 5 despite lack of dollar figures.

evidence_list.snippet: We have recently experienced, and expect to continue experiencing, reduced demand for certain of our products as a result of certain customers’ difficulty to obtain materials, components, and services due to disruptions in such customers’ supply chains.

components.reason: Reports actual decline in product demand tied to pandemic-driven supply problems.
Projects continuation of the issue.
Connects upstream customer constraints to company revenue risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct hit to demand and revenue potential warrants a mid-high score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: In April 2020, we suspended our operations in Mexicali, Mexico, for approximately two weeks pursuant to an order by the government of the state of Baja California, Mexico, resulting in a temporary reduction in our production levels.

components.reason: Provides a concrete historical shutdown event attributable to COVID-19 regulations.
Specifies duration (‘two weeks’) and production impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific plant closure with time frame shows significant realized operational disruption, scoring 6.

evidence_list.snippet: Over the course of the pandemic, we have implemented certain measures at our facilities worldwide in an effort to protect our employees’ health and well-being ... some of which have reduced the overall efficiency of our operations and increased manufacturing costs.

components.reason: Acknowledges protective measures that directly reduce efficiency and raise costs.
Presence of mitigation efforts indicates partial control.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows cost/efficiency drag but also reflects mitigation, giving it a modest score of 2.

evidence_list.snippet: Our implementation of these requirements may result in employee attrition, reduced employee morale, and difficulty securing future labor needs.

components.reason: Identifies forward-looking labor force risks stemming from pandemic-related vaccine mandates.
Risk is speculative and not yet realized.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Potential but un-realized HR risk keeps score low at 1.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced, and may continue to experience, reduced production capacity as a result of employee quarantines, absenteeism, and attrition, as well as restrictions on certain of our employees’ ability to work.

components.reason: Confirms actual production capacity reductions due to pandemic-driven labor issues.
Notes expectation of continued impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Documented production hit plus ongoing risk yields a score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced, and likely will continue to experience, disruptions to global transportation networks, limiting or delaying our ability, and/or increasing our cost, to send or receive products and materials at one or more of our facilities, including as a result of trade restrictions, border closures, disruptions in the operations of third-party carriers, or carriers’ decisions to prioritize other customers’ orders over ours.

components.reason: Details concrete logistics disruptions already felt.
Enumerates multiple causes (border closures, carrier prioritization).
Flags cost escalation as well as delays.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Operational and cost impacts across logistics justify a 5.

evidence_list.snippet: The resumption of normal business operations after any such interruptions may be delayed or constrained by lingering effects of the pandemic on our customers, suppliers, and other third-party service providers.

components.reason: Highlights prolonged recovery risk even after immediate disruptions end.
Statement is forward-looking and somewhat generic.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Future-oriented, high-level caution produces a minimal score of 1.

evidence_list.snippet: Even after the pandemic has subsided as a public health matter, we may experience material adverse impacts to our business as a result of its adverse impact on the global economy.

components.reason: Warns of lasting macro-economic effects on company performance.
No operational specifics or evidence yet of impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Macro-level risk with no specifics keeps score at 1.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic and the resulting economic downturn are affecting business conditions in our industry.

components.reason: Affirms present impact on entire industry, implying systemic risk.
Generic statement without company-specific detail.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Industry-level observation adds context but limited company granularity, scoring 1.

evidence_list.snippet: The semiconductor industry is experiencing various supply constraints due to the pandemic.

components.reason: Attributes ongoing supply constraints directly to COVID-19.
Statement is industry-wide and lacks company-specific impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: General supply-constraint note offers limited incremental risk detail, so score is 1.

evidence_list.snippet: The duration, severity, and future impact of the pandemic, including as a result of more contagious variants of the virus that causes COVID-19, continue to be highly uncertain and could still result in significant disruptions to our business operations, as well as negative impacts to our financial condition.

components.reason: Emphasizes uncertainty and potential for ‘significant disruptions’ to operations and finances.
Forward-looking with no numeric data.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Strong wording on possible future disruption but lacks quantification, leading to a score of 2.
